implementation_summary: Gated handleLeaveIntent's deps.enqueueLeave(ctx.groupId, payload.pubkey) call on payload.pubkey === sender.pubkey.toLowerCase() (AC-FORCE-3): a leave_intent whose message-BODY subject diverges from the message's authenticated sender (the S1 seam, threaded through as the handler's 3rd arg since S2) is now silently dropped before enqueueLeave — no removal enqueued, no departure side effect. The self-departure path (subject === sender) is unaffected: payload.pubkey is still passed through to enqueueLeave unchanged. parseLeaveIntent (leaveSync.ts) now canonicalizes the parsed pubkey to lowercase hex so the comparison is like-for-like against AuthenticatedSender.pubkey; the wire shape ({ pubkey: string } JSON) is unchanged. Added an inline comment on the gate documenting the AC-MV-1 readiness-only caveat: under the app-layer-only stub the attacker controls both payload.pubkey and sender.pubkey (directly, or via the dev-only override hook), so the gate does not yet stop a real forced removal — it becomes load-bearing once the out-of-scope MLS sender-binding backbone (ADR-012) feeds a true authenticated sender. Did not touch MarmotContext.fireAutoCommit (commit-time re-verification is an explicit Non-Goal — a separate follow-up) and made no change to the dispatcher choke-point (S1) or handler signature (S2).
